review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_of_reflects. The two theorems have the same proof, and the same shape occurs twice more in Preadditive/Yoneda/Projective.lean, so there are four copies in total. The reasoning in each copy is small: one existing lemma application plus one instance. The finding is therefore modest, and the case for it rests on removing four copies of the type-ascribed `refine` boilerplate. I did not check whether a general iff lemma already exists elsewhere. I did not check whether the proposed `exact` closes by defeq (`preadditiveYoneda.obj J ⋙ forget _` versus `yoneda.obj J`). I did not check whether `Functor.preservesEpimorphisms_comp` fires as an instance in the generic lemma.

findings.problem: Both theorems run the same argument. They rewrite with `injective_iff_preservesEpimorphisms_yoneda_obj`. They then prove `F ⋙ forget` preserves epis ↔ `F` preserves epis. The forward direction uses `preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_of_reflects`; the backward direction uses an `inferInstance` for the composite. Each copy needs a type-ascribed `fun h : ... => ?_` and a separate `intro`/`exact` branch just to name the composite. The same block appears twice more in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Preadditive/Yoneda/Projective.lean, for coyoneda. The proofs would otherwise be one-liners, and no general iff lemma exists for them to use.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a general lemma next to `Functor.preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_of_reflects` in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/EpiMono.lean, tagged `@[to_dual]` like its neighbours:

theorem Functor.preservesEpimorphisms_comp_iff_of_preserves_of_reflects (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) [G.PreservesEpimorphisms] [G.ReflectsEpimorphisms] : (F ⋙ G).PreservesEpimorphisms ↔ F.PreservesEpimorphisms

Proof sketch: `⟨fun _ => F.preservesEpimorphisms_of_preserves_of_reflects G, fun _ => inferInstance⟩`. The reverse direction needs the composition instance for `PreservesEpimorphisms`.

The two theorems here then become

`rw [injective_iff_preservesEpimorphisms_yoneda_obj]; exact Functor.preservesEpimorphisms_comp_iff_of_preserves_of_reflects (preadditiveYoneda.obj J) (forget AddCommGrpCat)`

and the same with `(preadditiveYonedaObj J) (forget (ModuleCat (End J)))`. The goal is `(yoneda.obj J).PreservesEpimorphisms ↔ ...`, so `exact` needs `preadditiveYoneda.obj J ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat` to unify with `yoneda.obj J` by defeq. If that fails, use `show`. The Projective.lean proofs shrink in the same way.
findings.benefit: Four near-identical blocks across two files collapse to a single reusable lemma. The two instance hypotheses (preserves and reflects epis for `forget`) are stated once instead of being hidden in `inferInstance` and ascription tricks. Each iff theorem becomes a short, direct reading of the mathematics. Any future change to the preserves/reflects argument is made in one place.
